title: Cross-Team Preflight: Dependency Contracts & Roadmap Cutover Checklists
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a lightweight, repeatable preflight framework for roadmap cutovers that bundles dependency contracts (owner, acceptance criteria, fallback) with a concise checklist for Eng/Design/Security/Infra. Goal: reduce last-minute cutover misses and post-cut defects by establishing agreed signals and a minimal gating flow.
background: Repeated cutover incidents in Q4 highlighted unclear ownership and late security/infra blockers.
Current dependency tracking lives in fragmented docs and retrospective decks; there is no standardized sign-off artifact attached to a release window.
PMs and Eng leads have asked for a short, enforceable preflight that is low-friction and integrates with existing Linear/Console workflows.
goals: Define a single-page 'Dependency Contract' template that enumerates owners, acceptance tests, fallbacks, and monitoring signals.
Ship a 'preflight checklist' workflow that PMs can require for any roadmap cutover with cross-team coupling > medium.
Automate visibility: surface contract status in the Roadmap dashboard and per-initiative Console card.
Reduce cutover emergency rollback rate by 40% in the first two quarters after rollout.
success_criteria: Template adopted by 80% of active initiatives in Cycle 2026-W12 or later.
Dashboard shows complete contract coverage for all P0/P1 releases.
Post-cutover incidents attributable to 'unresolved dependency' fall by >=40% vs baseline (Q4 2025).
scope: Design the Dependency Contract template and Preflight Checklist.
Publish Confluence + copy templates into Linear issue templates.
Add a single read-only column in the Roadmap dashboard that shows 'preflight status' (not full workflow automation).
Run a pilot with two initiatives (one infra-heavy, one product feature) and iterate on checklist items.
out_of_scope: Full end-to-end automation of approvals and gated CI/CD pipelines (follow-up project).
Replacing existing SLO or incident tooling; we will reference those sources but not migrate them.
stakeholders: Eng leads: Marcus Li (assignee), Priya Shah
approach: 1) Draft a concise Dependency Contract template (one page).
2) Convene a 60-minute cross-functional workshop to validate fields and acceptance signals.
3) Convert the contract into a Linear issue template and a Confluence form for asynchronous sign-offs.
4) Wire a 'status' field into the Roadmap dashboard (read-only) and add a small preflight panel to initiative pages.
5) Pilot with two initiatives, collect metrics and qualitative feedback, iterate, and then require for all P0/P1 releases.
milestones: 2026-03-10: Ticket created and initial draft contract attached (Confluence).
2026-03-18: Linear template and Confluence form published (pilot-ready).
2026-03-22: Roadmap dashboard read-only status column added (visual only).
2026-03-25: Pilot cutovers run with two initiatives; feedback survey deployed.
acceptance_criteria: Contract template exists in Confluence and a Linear issue template is present in the templates library.
Two pilot initiatives have completed a preflight and documented fallbacks and acceptance tests.
Roadmap dashboard surfaces preflight status for active initiatives and links back to the contract.
risks: Teams treat the preflight as checkbox compliance rather than an engineering signal — mitigated by short required acceptance tests and a follow-up review if tests are not automated.
Dashboard integration is delayed due to API rate limits on Console — mitigation: ship read-only links first, schedule automation in next cycle.
Overhead pushes small initiatives to skip preflight — mitigation: define an explicit threshold (cross-team coupling > medium) and allow opt-outs with PM justification.
open_questions: What minimum set of monitoring signals should be required for Security to mark a dependency 'green'? (SEC input requested)
Should infra-provided services require a separate 'capacity verification' entry in the contract?
How do we link contract acceptance to Code Owners or PR checks (lightweight suggestion vs enforcement)?
Who will own the org-level enforcement policy after pilot? PM Guild or Release Eng?
updates: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket and uploaded initial contract draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Preflight+Contracts
2026-03-11 - Marcus Li: Quick engineering review — suggested adding a short 'validated by' field for infra capacity and estimated verification steps.
2026-03-12 - Workshop notes: Security requested a required 'threat-surface' checkbox for public-facing features; Design asked for a UX rollback path to be included.

2026-03-13 - Decision: Keep template single-page; add three mandatory fields: owner, acceptance tests (1-3), fallback plan. PMs will mark a release 'preflight required' if cross-team coupling >= medium.
2026-03-13 - Marcus Li: Created pilot Linear templates and a draft PR to roadmap-tools repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/roadmap-tools/pull/83
links: GitHub: roadmap-tools PR with Linear template and README: https://github.com/redwood-inference/roadmap-tools/pull/83
notes: Trade-offs discussed: keep artifact terse to encourage completion vs. capturing enough context to be meaningful.
Longer-term automation (webhooks for status changes, gating in CI) is out-of-scope for this ticket but recommended for Q3 workstream.
Pilot success criteria intentionally pragmatic: adoption + measurable reduction in dependency-related rollbacks.
